FN-83BD22-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 145
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Sponsor: Senator Steve Livingston
Economic Development
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/26/2023
Senate Bill 145 as reported by the Committee on Fiscal Responsibility and Economic
Development amends the Volunteer Rescue Squad Tuition Reimbursement Act of 2018 to allow
the following: (1) allow for the additional reimbursement of fees to complete an approved
course; (2) reduce the service requirement of students from 3 to 2 years; (3) add ambulance
services to the list of organizations that qualify for a student to complete meet their service
requirement; (4) allow tuition and fee reimbursement to be paid to an association that funded a
student, and clarify that no reimbursement would be paid for grants given to a student by
another program; (5) allow an increase of operational expenses of the program from two percent
to ten percent of the funding for the program each fiscal year; and (6) allow the Alabama
Community College System (ACCS) to consider a retroactive reimbursement of actual tuition
costs, excluding fees, to an association that was denied reimburse previously.
Additionally, beginning in Fiscal Year 2024, this bill would require tuition reimbursement be
divided equally among students for volunteer fire departments, rescue squads, and
ambulance services based on available appropriations. Further, beginning Fiscal Year 2025, any
unexpended funds in excess of $500,000 would be transferred to the Alabama Fire College to
provide emergency medical service equipment and operational grants to volunteer fire
departments and rescue squads.
These changes would increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Community
College System, the University of South Alabama and the Alabama Fire College, which would
be offset by an additional $10,000 annually in allowable operational expenses to administer the
program. Additionally, it would increase the expenditures of the program by an undetermined
